resources.string: Enamel share of a crown cross-section

With outer radius r and enamel thickness t, the inner radius is r − t. Enamel share = 100 × [1 − ((r − t) / r)²], expressed as a percentage of the full cross-section. Inner tissue area = π × (r − t)².

Enamel covers the tooth crown. Dentin lies beneath the enamel, and pulp occupies the center of the tooth. This model shows a hypothetical circular slice of the crown with a uniform enamel ring; it combines the tissues inside the ring rather than drawing dentin and pulp separately. A thicker ring takes up a larger share at the same crown radius, while a larger radius gives the same thickness a smaller share. Both dimensions are invented for teaching, not measured or typical values. This model cannot diagnose dental conditions or estimate enamel loss for an individual.
The example enamel is the pale outer ring. Its thickness is marked along the radius. The center represents everything inside the enamel.
